title.zh: 卷二百九十六 列傳第一百八十四 孝義一
title.raw: 卷二百九十六 列傳第一百八十四 孝義一 Volume 296 Biographies 184: Filial Acts 1

sentences.zh: 孝弟之行，雖曰天性，豈不賴有教化哉。

translations.literal: Conduct of filial piety and fraternal duty, though called innate nature, how does it not depend on having instruction and transformation?
translations.idiomatic: Filial and fraternal conduct may be called inborn, yet it surely depends on instruction and moral cultivation as well.

sentences.zh: 自聖賢之道明，誼壁英君莫不汲汲以厚人倫、敦行義為正風俗之首務。

translations.literal: Since the Way of the sages and worthies was made clear, successive illustrious rulers have all been eager to thicken human relations and promote righteous conduct as the foremost task in rectifying customs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the teaching of the sages was fully clarified, ruler after ruler of outstanding virtue made it an urgent priority to strengthen human bonds and encourage righteous conduct as the first step in reforming public morals.

sentences.zh: 旌勸之典，賁於閭閻，下逮委巷。

translations.literal: The institutions of commendation and encouragement shone in neighborhood wards and reached even to winding back alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Honors and incentives for virtue were displayed in every ward and extended even into the humblest lanes.

sentences.zh: 布衣之氓、匹夫匹婦、兒童稚弱之微賤，行修於閨闥之中，而名顯於朝廷之上。

translations.literal: Commoners in plain cloth, humble men and women, and the slight and lowly among children and infants—if their conduct was cultivated within the inner quarters, their names could yet be displayed at court.
translations.idiomatic: Plain cloth commoners, ordinary husbands and wives, even the smallest children of the humblest families—when virtue was practiced within the household, fame could still reach the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 觀其至性所激，感天地，動神明，水不能濡，火不能爇，猛獸不能害，山川不能阻，名留天壤，行卓古今，足以扶樹道教，敦厲末俗，綱常由之不泯，氣化賴以維持。

translations.literal: Observing how their utmost sincerity stirred response, they moved Heaven and Earth and stirred the spirits; water could not soak them, fire could not burn them, fierce beasts could not harm them, mountains and rivers could not block them; their names remained in heaven and earth and their conduct stood above past and present—sufficient to uphold and plant the Way of teaching, to urge and sharpen declining custom, so that the constants of the age were thereby not extinguished and transforming influence was thereby maintained.
translations.idiomatic: When their utmost sincerity was aroused, it touched Heaven and Earth and moved the spirits: water could not drown them, fire could not consume them, wild beasts could not harm them, and mountains and rivers could not bar their way. Their names endured under heaven, their deeds towered above antiquity and the present, enough to uphold moral teaching, stiffen a lax age, keep the bonds of society from perishing, and sustain the transforming power of custom.

sentences.zh: 是以君子尚之，王政先焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the noble person esteems this, and royal government puts it first.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the gentleman honors such conduct, and good government makes it a priority.

sentences.zh: 至或刑政失平，復仇泄忿，或遭時不造，荒盜流離，誓九死以不回，冒白刃而弗顧。

translations.literal: Yet sometimes punishments and government were unbalanced, and revenge vented resentment; or the times were unpropitious, with famine, banditry, and displacement—yet they vowed not to turn back though facing nine deaths, and faced naked blades without flinching.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at times when justice failed and men took revenge to vent their wrath, or when misfortune brought famine, brigandage, and exile, they still vowed never to turn back though death came nine times over, and marched unflinching against naked steel.

sentences.zh: 時則有司之辜，民牧之咎，為民上者，當為之惻然動念。

translations.literal: At such times the fault lay with the officials in charge and with those who tended the people; rulers over the people ought to be moved to compassion on their account.
translations.idiomatic: In such cases the blame rested on local officials and on those charged with governing the people; anyone who held authority over the populace ought to be stirred to pity by their plight.

sentences.zh: 故史氏誌忠孝義烈之行，如恐弗及，非徒以發側陋之幽光，亦以覘世變，昭法戒焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the historians record deeds of loyalty, filial piety, righteousness, and fierce integrity as if fearing they might not keep pace—not only to bring forth the hidden light of the obscure and lowly, but also to observe changes in the age and make clear warnings in law.
translations.idiomatic: That is why historians record loyal, filial, righteous, and heroic deeds as though they could never catch them all—not merely to lift obscure virtue into the light, but also to read the signs of the times and set forth lessons for the law.

sentences.zh: 明太祖詔舉孝弟力田之士，又令府州縣正官以禮遣孝廉士至京師。

translations.literal: The founding emperor of Ming issued an edict to recommend men of filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming, and also ordered the chief officials of prefectures, departments, and counties to send filial and incorrupt candidates to the capital with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor ordered the recommendation of men distinguished for filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming, and directed prefectural, departmental, and county magistrates to escort filial and incorrupt candidates to the capital in due ceremonial form.

sentences.zh: 百官聞父母喪，不待報，得去官。

translations.literal: When officials of every rank heard of a parent's death, without awaiting report they were permitted to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: All officials, on hearing of a parent's death, were allowed to resign their posts at once without awaiting formal approval.

sentences.zh: 割股臥冰，傷生有禁。

translations.literal: Cutting flesh from the thigh and lying on ice—acts that harm life were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Self-mutilation such as cutting flesh from one's thigh to heal a parent, or lying on ice to procure medicine, was banned because such practices endangered life.

sentences.zh: 其後遇國家覃恩海內，輒以詔書從事。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever the state extended grace throughout the realm, edicts were promptly issued on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever the court proclaimed a general amnesty or grace throughout the empire, edicts on such matters were issued at once.

sentences.zh: 有司上禮部請旌者，歲不乏人，多者十數。

translations.literal: When local offices submitted requests to the Ministry of Rites for commendation, each year lacked no candidates; in some years there were as many as a dozen or more.
translations.idiomatic: Each year local authorities forwarded petitions to the Ministry of Rites for commendation, and candidates were never lacking; in busy years there might be ten or more.

sentences.zh: 激勸之道，綦云備矣。

translations.literal: The ways of stirring and encouraging were exceedingly complete.
translations.idiomatic: The means of encouragement and reward were, one might say, fully in place.

sentences.zh: 實錄所載，莫可殫述，今采其尤者輯為傳。

translations.literal: What the Veritable Records contain cannot be fully related; now the most outstanding cases are selected and compiled into biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records record more than can be told in full; here the most remarkable cases are gathered into biographical accounts.

sentences.zh: 余援《唐書》例，臚其姓氏如左。

translations.literal: Following the precedent of the Book of Tang, I set forth their surnames and names as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Book of Tang as a model, I list their names below.

sentences.zh: 其事親盡孝，或萬里尋親，或三年廬墓，或聞喪殞命，或負骨還鄉者，洪武時，則有麗水祝昆，上元徐真童、李某女，龍江衛丁歪頭，懷寧曹鏞、鏞妻王氏，徐州王僧兒，廣德姚觀壽，廣武衛陳禮關，桃源張註，江浦張二女勝奴，上海沈德，溧陽史以仁，丹徒唐川，邳州李英，北平東安王重，遵化張拾，保定顧仲禮，樂亭杜仁義妻韓氏，昌平劉驢兒，保定新城王興，祁陽郝安童，山東寧海姜瑜，汶上侯昱，孟縣李德，鞏縣給事中魏敏，登封王中，舞陽周炳，臨桂李文選。

sentences.zh: 而鈞州張宗魯以瞽子有孝行，十七年被旌。

translations.literal: Moreover, Junzhou Zhang Zonglu, because as a blind son he had filial conduct, was commended in the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhou's Zhang Zonglu, a blind son whose filial conduct was outstanding, received imperial commendation in the seventeenth year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 洪熙間，則有江陰越鉉。

translations.literal: During the Hongxi reign there was Jiangyin Yue Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the brief Hongxi reign, Jiangyin's Yue Xuan was honored.

sentences.zh: 宣德間，則有慶都邊靖，南樂康祥、楊鐸，內黃崔克昇，江寧張繼宗，定遠王絅，舒城錢敏，徐州衛張文友，歸德衛任貴，浮梁洪信文，堂邑趙巖，汶上馬威，翼城劉原真，太康順孫陳智，鈞州楊鼐，延安衛指揮王永、安嶽、李遇中。

sentences.zh: 弘治間，則有大興錢福，宛平序班夏琮，青縣張俸，南和張彪，曲周趙象賢，長垣王鼐，開州甘潤、馬宗範，薊州孟振，遷安韓廷玉，元氏王懋，深州王寧，天津衛鄭海，武平衛王矩，廣寧右衛李周，霍丘徐汝楫，海州定邊衛經歷徐謐，邳州丁友，懷遠徐本忠、劉澄，宣城吳宗周，潁上王翊，鳳陽衛張全，鳳陽張欽、王澄，嘉定縣沈輔、沈呈，昆山徐協祥，豐縣周潭，徐州權宇、楊輔，績谿許欽，英山段弘仁，六安張時厚，蕭縣唐鸞、南傑，錢塘朱昌，仁和陳璋、璋妻錢氏，余姚黃濟之，桐廬王瑁，江西樂安謝紳，南昌左衛黃璉，安福劉珍，豐城余壽，湖廣寧鄉同知劉端，湘陰甘準，祁陽張機，閩縣高惟一，龍谿王彜，濟南序班谷珍，莘縣白溥，鄒平辛恕，堂邑李尚質，益都冀琮，文登致仕縣丞劉鑒，臨清王祐，寧海州卜懷，陵川徐河、徐瑛，平遙趙澄，澤州宋甫、裴春、舉人李用，興縣白好古，解州李錦，陽曲薛敬，榆次趙復性，屯留衛李清，儀封謝欽，祥符陳鎧、周府儀賓史經，西平張文佐，河南唐縣李擴，登封王祺，嵩縣杜端，裕州劉宗周，閿鄉薛璋，洛陽護衛軍余章瀚，鈞州陣希全，新鄭張遂，郟縣黃錦，鹹寧舉人楊時敷，涇陽熊玻、張憲，隴西李琦，甘州後衛徐行，博羅何宇新，雲南芮城李錦及子澤、澤子柄，太和楊謫仙，靖安陳伯瑄及子恩。

sentences.zh: 萬歷間，則有直隸韓錫，深州林基，井陘張民望，清豐侯燦，河間吳應奎，平山舉人邢雲衢，邳州張縝，直隸華亭楊應祈、高承順，太湖顧槐，盱眙蔣臚，六安何金，遂安毛存元，江西余鑰、徐信，都昌曹珊，萬安劉靜，新建樊儆、舒泰，會昌歐於復，鄱陽李岐，奉新周勃，南昌曹必和，湖廣賈應進，光化蔡玉、蔡佩，黃岡唐治，浦城徐彪，泉州訓導王熺及熺子文升，晉江韋起宗，山東馬致遠，冠縣申一琴、一攀，嶽陽王應科，河南侯鶴齡，歸德賈洙，密縣陳邦寵，舞陽楊愈光，汜水王謙，淅川劉待徵，陜西劉燧，涇陽韓汝復，寧州周大賢，成都後衛楊茂勛，井研曾海，大姚金鯉，蒙化範潤，四川孝女解氏。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign there were Zhili Han Xi, Shenzhou Lin Ji, Jingxing Zhang Minwang, Qingfeng Hou Can, Hejian Wu Yingkui, Pingshan provincial graduate Xing Yunqu, Pizhou Zhang Chen, Zhili Huating Yang Yingqi and Gao Chengshun, Taihu Gu Huai, Xuyi Jiang Lu, Lu'an He Jin, Suian Mao Cunyuan, Jiangxi Yu Yao and Xu Xin, Duchang Cao Shan, Wan'an Liu Jing, Xinjian Fan Jing and Shu Tai, Huichang Ou Yufu, Poyang Li Qi, Fengxin Zhou Bo, Nanchang Cao Bihe, Huguang Jia Yingjin, Guanghua Cai Yu and Cai Pei, Huanggang Tang Zhi, Pucheng Xu Biao, Quanzhou instructor Wang Xi and Xi's son Wensheng, Jinjiang Wei Qizong, Shandong Ma Zhiyuan, Guan County Shen Yiqin and Yi Pan, Yueyang Wang Yingke, Henan Hou Heling, Guide Jia Zhu, Mi County Chen Bangchong, Wuyang Yang Yuguang, Qishui Wang Qian, Xichuan Liu Daizheng, Shaanxi Liu Sui, Jingyang Han Rufu, Ningzhou Zhou Daxian, Chengdu Rear Guard Yang Maoxun, Jingyan Zeng Hai, Dayao Jin Li, Menghua Fan Run, and Sichuan filial daughter née Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli produced Zhili's Han Xi; Shenzhou's Lin Ji; Jingxing's Zhang Minwang; Qingfeng's Hou Can; Hejian's Wu Yingkui; Pingshan graduate Xing Yunqu; Pizhou's Zhang Chen; Zhili Huating's Yang Yingqi and Gao Chengshun; Taihu's Gu Huai; Xuyi's Jiang Lu; Lu'an's He Jin; Suian's Mao Cunyuan; Jiangxi's Yu Yao and Xu Xin; Duchang's Cao Shan; Wan'an's Liu Jing; Xinjian's Fan Jing and Shu Tai; Huichang's Ou Yufu; Poyang's Li Qi; Fengxin's Zhou Bo; Nanchang's Cao Bihe; Huguang's Jia Yingjin; Guanghua's Cai Yu and Cai Pei; Huanggang's Tang Zhi; Pucheng's Xu Biao; Quanzhou instructor Wang Xi and his son Wensheng; Jinjiang's Wei Qizong; Shandong's Ma Zhiyuan; Guan County's Shen Yiqin and Yi Pan; Yueyang's Wang Yingke; Henan's Hou Heling; Guide's Jia Zhu; Mi County's Chen Bangchong; Wuyang's Yang Yuguang; Qishui's Wang Qian; Xichuan's Liu Daizheng; Shaanxi's Liu Sui; Jingyang's Han Rufu; Ningzhou's Zhou Daxian; Chengdu Rear Guard's Yang Maoxun; Jingyan's Zeng Hai; Dayao's Jin Li; Menghua's Fan Run; and Sichuan's filial daughter née Jie.

sentences.zh: 又有馬錦、張浩、杜惠、孝女楊氏等，不詳邑裏。

translations.literal: There were also Ma Jin, Zhang Hao, Du Hui, filial daughter née Yang, and others whose native places are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Also honored were Ma Jin, Zhang Hao, Du Hui, filial daughter née Yang, and others whose home districts the records do not specify.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，則有安州邵桂，棗強先自正，晉州張蘭，高邑孫喬，上海張秉介，高淳葛至學，旌德江景宗，山陽張致中，歙縣吳榮讓、孝童女胡之憲、玉娥，慈谿馮象臨，吉水郭元達，宜春鐘名揚，峽江黃國賓，臨川傅合，萬載彭夢瑞，南康楊可幸，萬安羅應賫，江西樂安曹希和，安福孝婦王三重妻謝氏，孝感施文星，福建李躍龍，甌寧陳榮，晉江丘應賓，浦城吳昂，禹城給事中楊士衡，泰安範希賢，曹縣王治寧，曲阜孔弘傳，德州紀紹堯，聞喜張學孔，陳州郭一肖，虞城呂桂芳，淅川何大縉，華州孫繩祖，梁山李資孝，又有王錫光不詳邑裏。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign there were Anzhou Shao Gui, Zaoqiang Xian Zizheng, Jinzhou Zhang Lan, Gaoyi Sun Qiao, Shanghai Zhang Bingjie, Gaochun Ge Zhixue, Jingde Jiang Jingzong, Shanyang Zhang Zhizhong, She County Wu Rongrang, filial child Hu Zhixian and Yue'e, Cixi Feng Xianglin, Jishui Guo Yuanda, Yichun Zhong Mingyang, Xiajiang Huang Guobin, Linchuan Fu He, Wanzai Peng Mengrui, Nankang Yang Kexing, Wan'an Luo Yingbin, Jiangxi Le'an Cao Xihe, Anfu filial wife Wang Sanzhong's wife née Xie, Xiaogan Shi Wenxing, Fujian Li Yuelong, Ouning Chen Rong, Jinjiang Qiu Yingbin, Pucheng Wu Ang, Yucheng supervising secretary Yang Shiheng, Tai'an Fan Xixian, Cao County Wang Zhining, Qufu Kong Hongchuan, Dezhou Ji Shaoyao, Wenxi Zhang Xuekong, Chenzhou Guo Yixiao, Yucheng Lü Guifang, Xichuan He Dajin, Huazhou Sun Shengzu, Liangshan Li Zixiao, and also Wang Xiguang, whose native place is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi saw Anzhou's Shao Gui; Zaoqiang's Xian Zizheng; Jinzhou's Zhang Lan; Gaoyi's Sun Qiao; Shanghai's Zhang Bingjie; Gaochun's Ge Zhixue; Jingde's Jiang Jingzong; Shanyang's Zhang Zhizhong; She County's Wu Rongrang, filial child Hu Zhixian, and Yue'e; Cixi's Feng Xianglin; Jishui's Guo Yuanda; Yichun's Zhong Mingyang; Xiajiang's Huang Guobin; Linchuan's Fu He; Wanzai's Peng Mengrui; Nankang's Yang Kexing; Wan'an's Luo Yingbin; Jiangxi Le'an's Cao Xihe; Anfu filial wife Wang Sanzhong's wife née Xie; Xiaogan's Shi Wenxing; Fujian's Li Yuelong; Ouning's Chen Rong; Jinjiang's Qiu Yingbin; Pucheng's Wu Ang; Yucheng supervising secretary Yang Shiheng; Tai'an's Fan Xixian; Cao County's Wang Zhining; Qufu's Kong Hongchuan; Dezhou's Ji Shaoyao; Wenxi's Zhang Xuekong; Chenzhou's Guo Yixiao; Yucheng's Lü Guifang; Xichuan's He Dajin; Huazhou's Sun Shengzu; Liangshan's Li Zixiao; and Wang Xiguang, whose district is likewise unspecified.

sentences.zh: 崇禎間，則有應天王之卿，故城李華先，仁和沈尚誌，江西王之範，福建吳宗烜，山東朱文龍，忻州趙裕心，稷山舉人史宗禹，淳化高起鳳，雲南趙文宿。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign there were Yingtian Wang Zhiqing, Gucheng Li Huaxian, Renhe Shen Shangzhi, Jiangxi Wang Zhifan, Fujian Wu Zongxuan, Shandong Zhu Wenlong, Xinzhou Zhao Yuxin, Jishan provincial graduate Shi Zongyu, Chunhua Gao Qifeng, and Yunnan Zhao Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen's roll included Yingtian's Wang Zhiqing; Gucheng's Li Huaxian; Renhe's Shen Shangzhi; Jiangxi's Wang Zhifan; Fujian's Wu Zongxuan; Shandong's Zhu Wenlong; Xinzhou's Zhao Yuxin; Jishan graduate Shi Zongyu; Chunhua's Gao Qifeng; and Yunnan's Zhao Wensu.

sentences.zh: 又有王宅中、任萬庫、武世捷、孔維章、浦某、褚鹹、孫良輔等，不詳邑裏。

translations.literal: There were also Wang Zaizhong, Ren Wanku, Wu Shijie, Kong Weizhang, Pu Mou, Chu Xian, Sun Liangfu, and others whose native places are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Also listed were Wang Zaizhong, Ren Wanku, Wu Shijie, Kong Weizhang, Pu Mou, Chu Xian, Sun Liangfu, and others whose home districts remain unspecified.

sentences.zh: 皆以孝行旌其門。

translations.literal: All were commended at their gates for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Each received gate commendation for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 其同居敦睦者，則有洪武時龍遊夏文昭，四世同居。

translations.literal: As for those who dwelt together in harmony, during Hongwu there was Longyou Xia Wenzhao, four generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Among households that lived together in harmony, Hongwu produced Longyou's Xia Wenzhao, whose clan shared one roof for four generations.

sentences.zh: 成化間，霸州秦貴，建德何永敬，蒲圻李玘，句容戴睿，饒陽耿寬，俱七世同居，石首王宗義五世同爨，宿遷張賓八世同爨，安東蘇勒，潞城韓錦、李昇，永州唐汝賢，豐城劉誌清，俱六世同居。

translations.literal: During Chenghua there were Bazhou Qin Gui, Jiande He Yongjing, Puqi Li Zhi, Jurong Dai Rui, and Raoyang Geng Kuan, all seven generations dwelling together; Shishou Wang Zongyi, five generations sharing one kitchen; Suqian Zhang Bin, eight generations sharing one kitchen; Andong Su Le; Lucheng Han Jin and Li Sheng; Yongzhou Tang Ruxian; and Fengcheng Liu Zhiqing, all six generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua saw Bazhou's Qin Gui, Jiande's He Yongjing, Puqi's Li Zhi, Jurong's Dai Rui, and Raoyang's Geng Kuan, each clan united for seven generations; Shishou's Wang Zongyi, five generations at one hearth; Suqian's Zhang Bin, eight generations at one hearth; Andong's Su Le; Lucheng's Han Jin and Li Sheng; Yongzhou's Tang Ruxian; and Fengcheng's Liu Zhiqing, each united for six generations.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，密雲李琚，合肥鄭元，陵川徐梁，安東朱勇，五世同居，慶都黃鐘，定邊衛韓鵬，俱六世同居，孝感程昂七世同居，泰州王玉八世同爨。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi there were Miyun Li Ju, Hefei Zheng Yuan, Lingchuan Xu Liang, and Andong Zhu Yong, five generations dwelling together; Qingdu Huang Zhong and Dingbian Guard Han Peng, both six generations dwelling together; Xiaogan Cheng Ang, seven generations dwelling together; and Taizhou Wang Yu, eight generations sharing one kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi produced Miyun's Li Ju, Hefei's Zheng Yuan, Lingchuan's Xu Liang, and Andong's Zhu Yong, five generations under one roof; Qingdu's Huang Zhong and Dingbian Guard's Han Peng, six generations each; Xiaogan's Cheng Ang, seven generations; and Taizhou's Wang Yu, eight generations at one hearth.

sentences.zh: 正德間，山陽丁震五世同居。

translations.literal: During Zhengde there was Shanyang Ding Zhen, five generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde added Shanyang's Ding Zhen, whose household endured five generations together.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，石偉十一世同居，遂安毛彥恭六世同居。

translations.literal: During Jiajing there was Shi Wei, eleven generations dwelling together, and Suian Mao Yangong, six generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing saw Shi Wei's clan united for eleven generations and Suian Mao Yangong's for six.

sentences.zh: 萬歷間，蕭梅七世同居，滁州盧守一，長治仇大，六世同居，先後得節烈貞女二十三人，太平楊乙六累世同居。

translations.literal: During Wanli, Xiao Mei dwelt together for seven generations; Chuzhou Lu Shouyi and Changzhi Qiu Da, six generations dwelling together, with twenty-three chaste and faithful women honored in succession; and Taiping Yang Yi, six successive generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli brought Xiao Mei's seven-generation household; Chuzhou's Lu Shouyi and Changzhi's Qiu Da, six generations each, with twenty-three women honored in turn for chastity and fidelity; and Taiping's Yang Yi, six successive generations united.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，南城吳煥八世同居。

translations.literal: During Tianqi there was Nancheng Wu Huan, eight generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi produced Nancheng's Wu Huan, eight generations under one roof.

sentences.zh: 皆旌曰義門。

translations.literal: All were commended as Gates of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Each received commendation as a Gate of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 其輸財助官振濟者，則有正統間千戶胡文郁，訓術李昺，訓科劉文勝，吉安胡有初、謝子寬，浮梁範孔孫，榆次於敏，邳州鞏得海、岑仲暉、高興、葉旺、高宗泰，沭陽葛禎，清河王仲英，山陽鮑越，懷遠廖冠平、張簡，石州張雷，淮安梁辟、李成、俞勝、徐成，潞州李廷玉，羅山王必通，溧陽陸旺，余幹舒彥祥，溫州李倫、鄒有真，四安何仕能、王清。

translations.literal: As for those who contributed wealth to assist officials in famine relief, during Zhengtong there were company commander Hu Wenyu, Xunshu Li Bing, Xunku Liu Wensheng, Ji'an Hu Youchu and Xie Zikuan, Fuliang Fan Kongsun, Yuci Yu Min, Pizhou Gong Dehai, Cen Zhonghui, Gao Xing, Ye Wang, and Gao Zongtai, Shuyang Ge Zhen, Qinghe Wang Zhongying, Shanyang Bao Yue, Huaiyuan Liao Guanping and Zhang Jian, Shizhou Zhang Lei, Huai'an Liang Pi, Li Cheng, Yu Sheng, and Xu Cheng, Luzhou Li Tingyu, Luoshan Wang Bitong, Liyang Lu Wang, Yugan Shu Yanxiang, Wenzhou Li Lun and Zou Youzhen, and Si'an He Shineng and Wang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who donated wealth to aid official famine relief, Zhengtong honored company commander Hu Wenyu; Xunshu Li Bing; Xunku Liu Wensheng; Ji'an's Hu Youchu and Xie Zikuan; Fuliang's Fan Kongsun; Yuci's Yu Min; Pizhou's Gong Dehai, Cen Zhonghui, Gao Xing, Ye Wang, and Gao Zongtai; Shuyang's Ge Zhen; Qinghe's Wang Zhongying; Shanyang's Bao Yue; Huaiyuan's Liao Guanping and Zhang Jian; Shizhou's Zhang Lei; Huai'an's Liang Pi, Li Cheng, Yu Sheng, and Xu Cheng; Luzhou's Li Tingyu; Luoshan's Wang Bitong; Liyang's Lu Wang; Yugan's Shu Yanxiang; Wenzhou's Li Lun and Zou Youzhen; and Si'an's He Shineng and Wang Qing.

sentences.zh: 景泰間，江陰陳安常。

translations.literal: During Jingtai there was Jiangyin Chen Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai added Jiangyin's Chen Anchang.

sentences.zh: 天順間，潮陽郭吾，太原栗仲仁，代州李斌。

translations.literal: During Tianshun there were Chaoyang Guo Wu, Taiyuan Li Zhongren, and Daizhou Li Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun saw Chaoyang's Guo Wu, Taiyuan's Li Zhongren, and Daizhou's Li Bin.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，歸善吳宗益、宗義及宗義子璋。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi there were Guishan Wu Zongyi, Wu Zongyi, and Wu Zongyi's son Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi produced Guishan's Wu Zongyi and Wu Zongyi, and Wu Zongyi's son Zhang.

sentences.zh: 隆慶間，永寧王潔、胥瓚。

translations.literal: During Longqing there were Yongning Wang Jie and Xu Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing added Yongning's Wang Jie and Xu Zan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷間，少卿吳炯，浙江董欽等，臨清張氏，江西胡士琇、丁果、婁世潔、黎金球，山西孫光勛、高自修，亳州李文明，順義楊惟孝。

translations.literal: During Wanli there were Vice Minister Wu Jiong, Zhejiang's Dong Qin and others, Linqing's Zhang clan, Jiangxi's Hu Shixiu, Ding Guo, Lou Shijie, and Li Jinqiu, Shanxi's Sun Guangxun and Gao Zixiu, Bozhou's Li Wenming, and Shunyi's Yang Weixiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli honored Vice Minister Wu Jiong; Zhejiang's Dong Qin and others; Linqing's Zhang clan; Jiangxi's Hu Shixiu, Ding Guo, Lou Shijie, and Li Jinqiu; Shanxi's Sun Guangxun and Gao Zixiu; Bozhou's Li Wenming; and Shunyi's Yang Weixiao.

sentences.zh: 天啟間南城吳煥。

translations.literal: During Tianqi there was Nancheng Wu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi again listed Nancheng's Wu Huan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎間席本楨等。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen there were Xi Benzhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen saw Xi Benzhen and others.

sentences.zh: 皆旌為義門，或賜璽書褒勞。

translations.literal: All were commended as Gates of Righteousness, or were granted sealed edicts of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Each was honored as a Gate of Righteousness, and some received sealed imperial writings of praise and reward.

translations.literal: Zheng Lian, courtesy name Zhongde, was a native of Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lian, styled Zhongde, came from Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 其家累世同居，幾三百年。

translations.literal: His family dwelt together for successive generations, nearly three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had lived together for generations, nearly three hundred years in all.

sentences.zh: 七世祖綺載《宋史·孝義傳》。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Qi is recorded in the "Treatise on Filial Acts" of the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Qi appears in the Treatise on Filial Acts of the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 六傳至文嗣，旌為義門，載《元史·孝友傳》。

translations.literal: Six generations later came Wensi, commended as a Gate of Righteousness and recorded in the "Treatise on Filial Friends" of the History of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations on, Wensi was honored as a Gate of Righteousness and entered the Treatise on Filial Friends of the History of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 弟文融，字太和，部使者余闕表為東浙第一家。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenrong, courtesy name Taihe, was acclaimed by the regional commissioner Yu Que as the foremost household in eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wenrong, styled Taihe, was proclaimed by regional commissioner Yu Que the foremost household in eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏家法，代以一人主家政。

translations.literal: The Zheng clan's household law held that each generation one person should preside over domestic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By Zheng family rule, one man in each generation directed the household.

sentences.zh: 文融卒，嗣子欽繼之，嘗刺血療本生父疾。

translations.literal: When Wenrong died, his heir son Qin succeeded him and once drew blood from his arm to treat the illness of his biological father.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenrong's death his heir Qin took charge and once lanced his arm to heal his birth father's sickness.

sentences.zh: 欽卒，弟鉅繼。

translations.literal: When Qin died, his younger brother Ju succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin died, his brother Ju assumed the role.

sentences.zh: 鉅卒，弟銘當主家政，以兄子渭宗子也，相讓久之，始受事。

translations.literal: When Ju died, his younger brother Ming was to preside over domestic affairs; because his elder brother's son Wei was the clan heir, they yielded to one another for a long time before Ming finally accepted the duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju died, brother Ming was due to head the household; because his elder brother's son Wei was the designated heir, the two deferred to each other at length before Ming at last took office.

sentences.zh: 銘受業於吳萊。

translations.literal: Ming studied under Wu Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Ming had studied under Wu Lai.

sentences.zh: 銘卒，弟鉉繼。

translations.literal: When Ming died, his younger brother Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Ming's death his brother Xuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 父喪，慟哭三日，發須盡白。

translations.literal: At his father's funeral he mourned with violent weeping for three days, and his beard and hair turned entirely white.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he wailed for three days until his beard and hair had turned wholly white.

sentences.zh: 元末兵起，大將數入其境，相戒無犯義門。

translations.literal: When warfare rose at the end of the Yuan, several great generals entered their territory and each warned his troops not to violate the Gate of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: As rebellion spread late in the Yuan, one great commander after another entered their lands, each ordering his men not to harm the Gate of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 樞密判官阿魯灰軍奪民財，鉉以利害折之，引去。

translations.literal: The Privy Council judge Aru Hui's army seized the people's property; Xuan argued the harm and benefit until he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Privy Council judge Aru Hui's troops plundered the people, Xuan confronted him with argument on profit and loss until the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明兵臨婺州，鉉挈家避，右丞李文忠為扃鑰其家，而遣兵護之歸。

translations.literal: Ming troops reached Wuzhou; Xuan led his family away in flight. Right Vice Minister Li Wenzhong locked and sealed his house and dispatched troops to escort them home.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces approached Wuzhou, Xuan moved his household to safety. Li Wenzhong, vice minister of the right, locked up the family residence and sent soldiers to bring them home under guard.

sentences.zh: 至正中卒，渭繼。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era he died; Wei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhizheng reign, and Wei took his place.

sentences.zh: 渭卒，弟濂繼。

translations.literal: When Wei died, his younger brother Lian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's death, his younger brother Lian assumed household leadership.

sentences.zh: 濂受知於太祖，昆弟由是顯。

translations.literal: Lian received the Founding Emperor's favor, and the brothers thereby became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Lian won the Founding Emperor's trust, and the brothers rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 濂以賦長詣京師，太祖問治家長久之道。

translations.literal: Lian, as head of the tax household, went to the capital; the Founding Emperor asked the way to keep a family long enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Lian traveled to the capital in his capacity as village head; the Founding Emperor asked him how a family might endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「謹守祖訓，不聽婦言。」

translations.literal: He replied, saying, "Strictly keep the ancestral instructions and do not heed women's words."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Hold fast to the ancestral rules and pay no heed to women's counsel."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，賜之果，濂拜賜懷歸，剖分家人。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it as good and bestowed fruit; Lian bowed, received the gift in his bosom, returned home, and divided it among the family.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and gave him fruit. Lian bowed, tucked the gift in his robe, went home, and shared it with the whole family.

sentences.zh: 帝聞嘉嘆，欲官之，以老辭。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and sighed in admiration, wishing to give him office; he declined on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this he sighed in admiration and offered him an appointment, but Lian refused on grounds of old age.

sentences.zh: 時富室多以罪傾宗，而鄭氏數千指獨完。

translations.literal: At the time many wealthy houses were ruined on criminal charges, but the Zheng clan alone, numbering thousands of mouths, remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: In those days wealthy clans were often destroyed on criminal charges, yet the Zheng household alone—thousands strong—remained intact.

sentences.zh: 會胡惟庸以罪誅，有訴鄭氏交通者，吏捕之，兄弟六人爭欲行，濂弟湜竟往。

translations.literal: When Hu Weiyong was executed for crime, someone accused the Zheng clan of collusion; officers came to arrest them. Six brothers each vied to go; Lian's younger brother Shi went in the end.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Weiyong was put to death, an informer charged the Zhengs with treasonous contact. Officers came to seize them. Six brothers each insisted on going; in the end Lian's younger brother Shi went.

sentences.zh: 時濂在京師，迎謂曰：「吾居長，當任罪。」

translations.literal: Lian was then in the capital and met him, saying, "I am the eldest and ought to bear the crime."
translations.idiomatic: Lian was in the capital at the time and met him on the way. "I am the eldest," he said. "The guilt should be mine."

sentences.zh: 湜曰：「兄年老，吾自往辨。」

translations.literal: Shi said, "Elder brother, you are old; I will go myself to plead the case."
translations.idiomatic: "You are old, brother," Shi replied. "I will go and argue the matter myself."

sentences.zh: 二人爭入獄。

translations.literal: The two struggled to enter prison.
translations.idiomatic: The two of them fought over who would enter the jail.

sentences.zh: 太祖召見曰：「有人如此，肯從人為逆耶？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned and saw them, saying, "When men are like this, would they willingly follow others in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor summoned them and said, "Men like this—would they ever willingly follow another in treason?"

sentences.zh: 宥之，立擢湜為左參議，命舉所知。

translations.literal: He pardoned them and at once promoted Shi to Left Participation Councilor, ordering him to recommend those he knew.
translations.idiomatic: He released them, immediately promoted Shi to Left Participation Councilor, and told him to recommend men he knew.

sentences.zh: 湜舉同郡王應等五人，皆授參議。

translations.literal: Shi recommended five men of the same commandery, including Wang Ying, and all were appointed Participation Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Shi nominated five men from his commandery, among them Wang Ying, and all five were made participation councilors.

sentences.zh: 湜，字仲持，居官有政聲。

translations.literal: Shi, courtesy name Zhongchi, had a reputation for good governance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Zhongchi, earned a reputation for effective government.

sentences.zh: 南靖民為亂，詿誤者數百家，湜言於諸將，盡釋免。

translations.literal: When the people of Nanjing rebelled, several hundred households were implicated by mistake; Shi spoke to the generals and all were released and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing county rose in revolt, several hundred families were caught up by mistake. Shi persuaded the generals to release them all.

sentences.zh: 居一歲，入覲，卒於京。

translations.literal: After one year he entered court for audience and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he came to court for an audience and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十九年，濂坐事當逮，從弟洧曰：「吾家稱義門，先世有兄代弟死者，吾可不代兄死乎？」

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Lian was implicated and due for arrest; his cousin Wei said, "Our house is called the Gate of Righteousness; in former generations brothers died in place of brothers—can I not die in my elder brother's stead?"
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Lian was implicated and faced arrest. His cousin Wei said, "Our clan is known as the Gate of Righteousness. Ancestors have died in a brother's place—why should I not die for my elder brother?"

sentences.zh: 詣吏自誣服，斬於市。

translations.literal: He went to the officers and falsely confessed guilt; he was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the magistrates, confessed falsely, and was beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 洧，字仲宗，受業於宋濂，有學行，鄉人哀之，私謚貞義處士。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Zhongzong, studied under Song Lian, had learning and conduct; the villagers mourned him and privately gave him the posthumous title Recluse of Loyal Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Zhongzong, had studied under Song Lian and was a man of learning and integrity. The countryside mourned him and privately styled him the Recluse of Loyal Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 初，渶嘗仕元為浙江行省宣使，主家政數年。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ying had once served the Yuan as Pacification Commissioner of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat and directed household affairs for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ying had served the Yuan as pacification commissioner of the Zhejiang branch secretariat and managed the household for several years.

sentences.zh: 建文帝表其門，渶朝謝，禦書「孝義家」三字賜之。

translations.literal: The Jianwen Emperor honored his gate; Ying came to court to give thanks, and the Emperor personally wrote the three characters "House of Filial Piety and Righteousness" as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianwen Emperor honored his gate. Ying came to court to give thanks, and the emperor wrote with his own hand the three words "House of Filial Piety and Righteousness" and bestowed them.

sentences.zh: 燕兵既入，有告建文帝匿其家者，遣人索之。

translations.literal: After the Yan army had entered, someone reported that the Jianwen Emperor was hidden in his household; men were sent to search.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yan armies entered the capital, someone reported that the Jianwen Emperor was concealed in his home, and searchers were sent.

sentences.zh: 渶家廳事中，列十大櫃，五貯經史，五貯兵器備不虞。

translations.literal: In the central hall of Ying's home stood ten large cabinets—five storing the Classics and histories, five storing weapons against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall of Ying's house stood ten great chests: five held the Classics and histories, five held arms against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 使者至，所發皆經史，置其半不啟，乃免於禍，人以為至行所感雲。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, every chest opened proved to hold Classics and histories; half were left unopened, and they thus escaped calamity—people held it the effect of utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys came, every chest they opened held only books. They left the rest unopened, and the family escaped harm—people said it was the reward of supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，有司奏鄭永朝世敦行義，復旌以孝義之門。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua, the local authorities reported that Zheng Yongchao's family for generations had practiced righteousness, and again honored their gate as Gate of Filial Piety and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chenghua the local office reported that Zheng Yongchao's line had for generations upheld righteous conduct, and again honored their gate as a Gate of Filial Piety and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 自文融至渶，皆以篤行著。

translations.literal: From Wenrong to Ying, all were known for sincere conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From Wenrong down to Ying, each was noted for steadfast moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 文融著《家範》三卷，凡五十八則，子欽增七十則，從子鉉又增九十二則，至濂弟濤與從弟泳、澳、湜，白於兄濂、源，共相損益，定為一百六十八則，刊行焉。

translations.literal: Wenrong wrote 《Family Standards》 in three scrolls, fifty-eight items in all; his son Qin added seventy items, and nephew Xuan added ninety-two more. When Lian's younger brother Tao and cousins Yong, Ao, and Shi informed their elder brothers Lian and Yuan, they revised together and fixed one hundred sixty-eight items, which were printed and circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrong composed 《Family Standards》 in three juan—fifty-eight precepts in all. His son Qin added seventy; his nephew Xuan added ninety-two more. Lian's younger brother Tao and his cousins Yong, Ao, and Shi consulted their elder brothers Lian and Yuan, revised the text together, and settled on one hundred sixty-eight precepts, which they published.

sentences.zh: 王澄，字德輝，亦浦江人。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng, courtesy name Dehui, was also from Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, styled Dehui, was likewise a man of Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 歲儉，出粟貸人，不取其息。

translations.literal: In years of scarcity he lent grain to others and took no interest.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years he lent grain to neighbors and charged no interest.

sentences.zh: 有鬻產者，必增直以足之。

translations.literal: When someone sold property, he always added to the price to make it sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: If someone had to sell land, he always added to the price so the seller would have enough.

sentences.zh: 慕義門鄭氏風，將終，集子孫誨之曰：「汝曹能合食同居如鄭氏，吾死目瞑矣。」

translations.literal: Admiring the manner of the Gate of Righteousness Zheng clan, as he neared death he gathered his descendants and instructed them, saying, "You can eat and dwell together as one household like the Zheng clan, and my eyes will close in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Admiring the Zheng clan's Gate of Righteousness, he gathered his descendants as death approached and told them, "If you can eat from one pot and live under one roof like the Zhengs, I shall die content."

sentences.zh: 子孫鹹拜受教。

translations.literal: The descendants all bowed and received the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: All his descendants bowed and accepted his charge.

sentences.zh: 澄生三子子覺、子麟、子偉，克承父誌。

translations.literal: Cheng had three sons—Jue, Lin, and Wei—who were able to carry out their father's aim.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had three sons—Jue, Lin, and Wei—who fulfilled their father's wish.

sentences.zh: 子覺生應，即為鄭湜所舉擢參議者。

translations.literal: Jue's son was Ying—the one Shi recommended and promoted to Participation Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Jue's son Ying was the Wang Ying whom Zheng Shi recommended and raised to participation councilor.

sentences.zh: 子偉生懃，即與鄭濟並擢庶子者。

translations.literal: Wei's son was Qin—the one promoted together with Zheng Ji to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Qin was the man promoted to junior tutor alongside Zheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 義門王氏之名，遂埒鄭氏。

translations.literal: The name of the Gate of Righteousness Wang clan thus came to equal the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang Gate of Righteousness thus came to stand on a par with the Zhengs.

sentences.zh: 又有王燾者，蘄水人，七世同居，一家二百余口，人無間言。

translations.literal: There was also a Wang Shen, a native of Qishui; seven generations dwelt together, one household of more than two hundred mouths, and no one spoke ill of another.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang Shen of Qishui: seven generations under one roof, more than two hundred mouths in a single household, and not a whisper of discord.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年十一月，詔旌為孝義之門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Hongwu, an edict honored them as Gate of Filial Piety and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Hongwu's ninth year an edict honored them as a Gate of Filial Piety and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 徐允讓，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Xu Yunrang was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yunrang came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 元末，賊起，奉父安走避山谷間。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, brigands rose; he led his father An in flight to the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out at the end of the Yuan, he took his father An and fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，欲斫安頸。

translations.literal: They met bandits who wished to cut An's neck.
translations.idiomatic: They met bandits who were about to strike An's neck.

sentences.zh: 允讓大呼曰：「寧殺我，勿殺我父！」

translations.literal: Yunrang shouted, "Better kill me—do not kill my father!"
translations.idiomatic: Yunrang cried out, "Kill me instead—spare my father!"

sentences.zh: 賊遂舍安殺允讓。

translations.literal: The bandits then released An and killed Yunrang.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits let An go and killed Yunrang.

sentences.zh: 將辱其妻潘，潘紿曰：「吾夫已死，從汝必矣。

translations.literal: They were about to dishonor his wife Pan; Pan deceived them, saying, "My husband is already dead; if I follow you, I surely will.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to violate his wife Pan. Pan deceived them: "My husband is dead. I will go with you—that much is certain.

sentences.zh: 若能焚吾夫，則無憾也。」

translations.literal: If you can cremate my husband, I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: But first burn my husband's body, and I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 賊許之，潘聚薪焚夫，投烈焰中死。

translations.literal: The bandits agreed; Pan gathered firewood, burned her husband, and threw herself into the blaze to die.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits agreed. Pan piled fuel, cremated her husband, then leapt into the flames and died.

sentences.zh: 賊驚嘆去，安獲全。

translations.literal: The bandits marveled, sighed, and left; An was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits marveled and withdrew. An survived unharmed.

sentences.zh: 洪武十六年，夫婦並旌。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Hongwu, husband and wife were both honored.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's sixteenth year husband and wife were both commended.

sentences.zh: 同時石永壽者，新昌人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Shi Yongshou, a native of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was Shi Yongshou of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 負老父避賊，賊執其父將殺之，號泣請代，賊殺永壽而去。

translations.literal: Carrying his aged father he fled from bandits; the bandits seized his father and were about to kill him. He wept and shouted, begging to take his place; the bandits killed Yongshou and went away.
translations.idiomatic: He was carrying his old father when bandits caught them. They seized the father to kill him. Yongshou wept and begged to die in his stead. The bandits killed Yongshou and left.

sentences.zh: 錢瑛，字可大，吉水人。

translations.literal: Qian Ying, courtesy name Keda, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ying, styled Keda, was from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 生八月而孤，年十三能應秋試。

translations.literal: Orphaned at eight months, at thirteen he could sit for the autumn examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was eight months old. At thirteen he could sit for the autumn examination.

sentences.zh: 及長，值元季亂，奉祖本和及母避難，歷五六年。

translations.literal: When grown, amid the chaos at the end of the Yuan, he escorted his grandfather Benhe and his mother in flight, for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult, in the turmoil at the end of the Yuan, he led his grandfather Benhe and his mother through five or six years of flight.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，縛本和，瑛奔救，並縛之。

translations.literal: They met bandits who bound Benhe; Ying ran to rescue and was bound together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits seized Benhe. Ying ran to save him and was bound as well.

sentences.zh: 本和哀告貰其孫，瑛泣請代不已，賊憐而兩釋之。

translations.literal: Benhe pleaded piteously to spare his grandson; Ying wept and begged without cease to take his place, and the bandits pitied them and released both.
translations.idiomatic: Benhe begged piteously that they spare his grandson. Ying wept and pleaded without end to die in his place. The bandits took pity and freed them both.

sentences.zh: 時瑛母亦被執，瑛妻張從伏莽中窺見，即趨出，謂賊曰：「姑老矣，請縛我。」

translations.literal: At the time Ying's mother was also seized; his wife Zhang, crouching in the scrub to watch, at once rushed out and said to the bandits, "My mother-in-law is old—please bind me instead."
translations.idiomatic: Ying's mother had also been taken. His wife Zhang had been hiding in the brush to watch. She ran forward and said to the bandits, "My mother-in-law is old. Bind me instead."

sentences.zh: 賊從之，既就縛，擲袖中鞋與姑，訣曰：「婦無用此矣。」

translations.literal: The bandits assented; once bound, she tossed shoes from her sleeve to her mother-in-law and bade farewell, saying, "Your daughter-in-law has no further use for these."
translations.idiomatic: They agreed. Once she was tied, she threw shoes from her sleeve to her mother-in-law and said farewell: "I have no more need of these."

sentences.zh: 且行且睨姑，稍遠即罵賊不肯行。

translations.literal: As she walked she glanced back at her mother-in-law; when a little distant she cursed the bandits for refusing to march.
translations.idiomatic: She walked on, glancing back at her mother-in-law. When she was some distance away she cursed the bandits for not moving faster.

sentences.zh: 賊持之急，罵益厲，賊怒，攢刃刺殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits hurried her; she cursed ever fiercer; the bandits in rage stabbed her to death with blades.
translations.idiomatic: They hurried her along. She cursed all the louder. Enraged, the bandits stabbed her to death.

sentences.zh: 是定，有司知瑛賢，凡三薦，並以親老辭。

translations.literal: Once the dynasty was settled, the authorities knowing Ying was worthy recommended him three times, and each time he declined on account of aged kin.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty was established, officials who knew his worth recommended him three times. Each time he declined because his elders were still alive.

sentences.zh: 子遂誌成進士，官山東僉事。

translations.literal: His son Sui became a metropolitan graduate and served as Regional Administration Vice Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sui passed the metropolitan examination and became vice commissioner in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同時曾鼎，字元友，泰和人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Zeng Ding, courtesy name Yuanyou, a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the same period there was Zeng Ding, styled Yuanyou, of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 祖懷可、父思立，並有學行。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huaike and father Silu both had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huaike and his father Silu were both men of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 元末，鼎奉母避賊。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, Ding escorted his mother to flee from bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, Ding fled with his mother from bandits.

sentences.zh: 母被執，鼎跪而泣請代。

translations.literal: When his mother was seized, Ding knelt and wept, begging to take her place.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was captured, Ding knelt and wept, begging to die in her stead.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，將殺母，鼎號呼以身翼蔽，傷頂肩及足，控母不舍。

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry and were about to kill his mother; Ding cried out and shielded her with his body, wounding his head, shoulders, and feet, yet would not release his grip on her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits grew angry and were about to kill her. Ding shouted and covered her with his body. They wounded his head, shoulders, and feet, but he would not let go.

sentences.zh: 賊魁繼至，憫之，攜其母子入營療治，獲愈。

translations.literal: The bandit chief came after and pitied them, carrying mother and son into the camp for treatment; they recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chief arrived, took pity, and brought mother and son into the camp to be treated. Both recovered.

sentences.zh: 行省聞其賢，辟為濂谿書院山長。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat, hearing of his worth, engaged him as mountain chief of Lianxi Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat, hearing of his virtue, appointed him mountain chief of Lianxi Academy.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，知縣郝思讓辟教設學。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, Magistrate Hao Sirang engaged him to establish teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's third year Magistrate Hao Sirang recruited him to set up local schooling.

sentences.zh: 鼎好學能詩，兼工八分及邵子數學。

translations.literal: Ding loved learning and could compose verse; he was also skilled in clerical script and Master Shao's numerological studies.
translations.idiomatic: Ding loved learning and wrote poetry. He was also accomplished in clerical script and the numerology of Master Shao.

sentences.zh: 姚玭，松江人。

translations.literal: Yao Pin was a native of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Pin was from Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 元至正中，苗帥楊完者兵入境。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era of the Yuan, Miao commander Yang Wanzhe's troops entered the district.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhizheng era, the Miao commander Yang Wanzhe's army entered the region.

sentences.zh: 比奉母避於野，阻河不可渡。

translations.literal: Bi led his mother to flee in the wilds; a river blocked them and they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bi took his mother to flee in the countryside. A river barred their way and they could not cross.

sentences.zh: 母泣曰：「兵至，吾誓不受辱。」

translations.literal: His mother wept, saying, "When the soldiers come, I vow not to suffer disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: His mother wept and said, "When the soldiers come, I will not live to be shamed."

sentences.zh: 遂沈於水。

translations.literal: She then sank into the water.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the water.

sentences.zh: 比急投水救之，負母而出。

translations.literal: Bi hastily threw himself into the water to save her and bore his mother out.
translations.idiomatic: Bi plunged in after her, pulled her out, and carried her on his back to safety.

sentences.zh: 已，數遇盜，中矢，比佯死伏屍間以免，以奉母過湖、淮。

translations.literal: Afterward they met bandits many times; he was struck by an arrow. Bi feigned death and lay among the corpses to escape, thereby escorting his mother across Lake Tai and the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Later they met bandits again and again. He took an arrow. Bi played dead among the slain and so survived, bringing his mother across the lakes and the Huai.

sentences.zh: 後母疾思食魚，暮夜無從得，家養一烏，忽飛去攫魚以歸。

translations.literal: Later when his mother fell ill and longed for fish, at night there was no way to obtain any; a crow they kept at home suddenly flew off, seized a fish, and brought it back.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother later fell ill and craved fish, none could be found at night. A crow they kept at home suddenly flew off, caught a fish, and brought it back.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，行省聞其賢，辟之，以親老不就。

translations.literal: In the early Hongwu period the Branch Secretariat, hearing of his worth, engaged him, but he did not take office because his kin were aged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu the branch secretariat sought to employ him, but he refused office because his parents were old.

sentences.zh: 丘鐸，字文振，祥符人。

translations.literal: Qiu Duo, courtesy name Wenzhen, was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Duo, styled Wenzhen, was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 元末，父為湖廣儒學提舉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan his father was Confucian Learning Intendant of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan his father served as Huguang intendant of Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 值兵亂，鐸奉父母播遷，賣藥供甘旨。

translations.literal: When warfare arose, Duo led his parents in wanderings and sold medicine to supply delicacies for them.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, Duo wandered with his parents and sold medicine to provide them fine food.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀慟幾絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his mourning nearly cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 葬鳴鳳山，結廬墓側，朝夕上食如生時。

translations.literal: He buried her at Mingfeng Mountain, built a hut beside the grave, and morning and evening offered food as when she lived.
translations.idiomatic: He buried her on Mingfeng Mountain, built a hut by the grave, and morning and evening set out food as though she were still alive.

sentences.zh: 當寒夜月黑，悲風蕭瑟，鐸輒繞墓號曰：「兒在斯！

translations.literal: On cold nights when the moon was black, with bleak wind sighing, Duo would circle the grave crying, "Your son is here!
translations.idiomatic: On bitter nights when the moon was dark and the wind mourned, Duo would pace the grave calling, "Your son is here!

sentences.zh: 兒在斯！」

translations.literal: Your son is here!"
translations.idiomatic: Your son is here!"

sentences.zh: 山深多虎，聞鐸哭聲避去。

translations.literal: Deep in the hills were many tigers, but hearing Duo's weeping they turned aside.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers were plentiful in those hills, yet at the sound of his weeping they kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 時稱真孝子。

translations.literal: The age called him a true filial son.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him a true filial son.

sentences.zh: 鐸初避寇慶元，從祖父母居故鄉者八人，貧不能自存，鐸悉迎養之。

translations.literal: When Duo first fled the bandits at Qingyuan, eight kin who had remained in the ancestral village with paternal grandparents could not support themselves in poverty; Duo brought them all in and provided for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo first fled bandits at Qingyuan, eight relatives who had stayed in the hometown with his grandparents were too poor to live. He brought them all in and supported them.

sentences.zh: 有姑年十八，夫亡守節，鐸養之終身。

translations.literal: He had a paternal aunt who at eighteen lost her husband and kept chastity; Duo supported her for life.
translations.idiomatic: He had a widowed aunt who at eighteen lost her husband and held to her chastity; Duo cared for her to the end of her days.

sentences.zh: 後有李茂者，澄城諸生也。

translations.literal: Later there was Li Mao, a licentiate of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Li Mao, a licentiate of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 母患惡瘡。

translations.literal: His mother suffered a malignant ulcer.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had a foul running sore.

sentences.zh: 茂日吮膿血，夜則叩天祈代。

translations.literal: Mao daily sucked out the pus and blood; at night he knocked heaven praying to take her illness upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Each day Mao sucked out the pus and blood. Each night he knelt and prayed heaven to give him her illness instead.

sentences.zh: 及卒，結廬墓旁，朝夕悲泣。

translations.literal: When she died, he built a hut beside the grave and wept morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he built a mourning hut by the grave and wept there morning and night.

sentences.zh: 天大雨，懼沖其墓，伏墓而哭，雨止乃已。

translations.literal: Heaven sent heavy rain; fearing it would wash out the grave, he lay on the tumulus weeping until the rain stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A great rain fell. Fearing it would wash away the mound, he lay on the grave and wept until the storm passed.

sentences.zh: 父卒，廬墓如之。

translations.literal: When his father died, he kept vigil at the grave in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he did the same.

sentences.zh: 成化二生旌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In 1466 he received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 二子表、森，森為國子生。

translations.literal: Two sons, Biao and Sen; Sen was a student at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Biao and Sen; Sen enrolled as a student at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 茂卒，兄弟同廬於墓。

translations.literal: When Mao died, the brothers together built mourning huts at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After Mao died, the brothers both lived in mourning huts beside his grave.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年旌。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi they were commended.
translations.idiomatic: In 1492 the court officially commended them.

sentences.zh: 表子俊亦國子生，表卒，俊方弱冠，廬墓終喪。

translations.literal: Biao's son Jun was also an Imperial Academy student; when Biao died, Jun had just reached weak-crown age and built a hut at the tomb through the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's son Jun was also at the Imperial Academy. When Biao died, Jun had only just come of age, yet he kept a mourning hut at the grave through the entire mourning term.

sentences.zh: 母卒，亦如初。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he did likewise as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he observed the same rites again.

sentences.zh: 正德四年旌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde they were commended.
translations.idiomatic: In 1509 he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 崔敏，字好學，襄陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Min, styled Haoxue, was a man of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Min, who went by Haoxue, came from Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 生四十日，其父仕元為綿竹尹，父子隔絕者三十年。

translations.literal: At forty days [after birth], his father served the Yuan as magistrate of Mianzhu; father and son were cut off from each other for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When he was forty days old, his father was already serving the Yuan as magistrate of Mianzhu, and father and son remained separated for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 敏依母兄以居。

translations.literal: Min relied on his mother and elder brother to live.
translations.idiomatic: Min lived with his mother and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 元季寇亂，母及兄俱相失。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan there was bandit turmoil; mother and elder brother both were lost from him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan collapsed into rebellion, he lost both his mother and his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 亂定，入陜尋母不得。

translations.literal: When the turmoil settled, he entered Shaanxi to seek his mother but did not obtain her.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned, he went into Shaanxi to find his mother, but could not.

sentences.zh: 由陜入川，抵綿竹，求父冢，無知者。

translations.literal: From Shaanxi he entered Sichuan, reached Mianzhu, sought his father's grave—no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled from Shaanxi into Sichuan, reached Mianzhu, and searched for his father's grave, but no one could tell him where it lay.

sentences.zh: 復還陜，訪諸親故，始知父殯所在，乃啟攢負骸歸。

translations.literal: He returned again to Shaanxi, visited all kin and old friends, and only then learned where his father's coffin lay; he opened the temporary burial, shouldered the bones, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Shaanxi he questioned every kinsman and old acquaintance until he learned where his father had been laid in temporary burial. He opened the grave, carried the bones home on his back, and buried them properly.

sentences.zh: 時稱崔孝子。

translations.literal: At the time he was called Filial Son Cui.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time called him Filial Son Cui.

sentences.zh: 同時劉鎬，江西龍泉人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Liu Hao, a man of Longquan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time there was Liu Hao of Longquan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 父允中，洪武五年舉人，官憑祥巡檢，卒於任。

translations.literal: His father Yunzhong, a juren of the fifth year of Hongwu, served as inspector of Pingxiang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunzhong had passed the provincial examination in 1372 and served as inspector of Pingxiang, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 鎬以道遠家貧，不能返柩，居常悲泣。

translations.literal: Hao, because the road was far and the family poor, could not return the coffin and constantly wept in grief while at home.
translations.idiomatic: The journey was too far and the family too poor for Hao to bring his father's body home, and he wept in grief day after day.

sentences.zh: 父友憐之，言於廣西監司，聘為臨桂訓導。

translations.literal: His father's friends pitied him and spoke to the Guangxi surveillance commissioner, who hired him as instructor at Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: His father's friends took pity on him and appealed to the Guangxi surveillance commissioner, who appointed him instructor at Lingui.

sentences.zh: 尋假公事赴憑祥，莫知葬處。

translations.literal: Soon he took official business as pretext to go to Pingxiang, but no one knew the burial place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he used official business as a pretext to reach Pingxiang, yet still no one knew where his father was buried.

sentences.zh: 鎬晝夜環哭，一蒼頭故從其父，已轉入交址。

translations.literal: Hao wept day and night around [the area]; an old attendant who had once followed his father had already been transferred into Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wept day and night as he searched the area. An old servant who had once attended his father had already been reassigned to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 忽暮至，若有憑之者，因得冢所在。

translations.literal: Suddenly at dusk he arrived, as if something were guiding him, and thereby found where the grave was.
translations.idiomatic: Then, at dusk, the old servant suddenly appeared, as though led by fate, and showed him where the grave stood.

sentences.zh: 刺血驗之良是，乃負歸葬。

translations.literal: He drew blood to verify—it was indeed correct—and then shouldered [the remains] home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Hao pricked his finger and let the blood fall on the bones to confirm they were his father's. Satisfied, he carried them home for burial.

sentences.zh: 有顧琇者，字季粟，吳縣人。

translations.literal: There was Gu Xiu, styled Jisu, a man of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Gu Xiu, known as Jisu, from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，父充軍鳳翔，母隨行，留琇守丘墓。

translations.literal: Early in Hongwu his father was conscripted to military service at Fengxiang; his mother went with him, leaving Xiu to guard the family graves.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign his father was conscripted to military service at Fengxiang. His mother went with him, leaving Xiu behind to tend the family graves.

sentences.zh: 越六年，母歿。

translations.literal: After six years his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later his mother died.

sentences.zh: 琇奔赴，負母骨行數千里，寢則懸之屋梁，涉則戴之於頂。

translations.literal: Xiu rushed to her, shouldered his mother's bones and traveled several thousand li; when he slept he hung them from the roof beam, when he waded he wore them on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu hurried to her side, gathered her bones, and carried them thousands of li homeward. When he slept he hung the bundle from a roof beam; when he crossed water he bore it on his head.

sentences.zh: 父釋歸卒。

translations.literal: His father was released and returned, then died.
translations.idiomatic: His father was eventually released and came home, but soon died.

sentences.zh: 水漿不入口五日，不勝喪而死。

translations.literal: For five days he took neither water nor broth; unable to bear his grief, he died.
translations.idiomatic: For five days he refused food and drink, and grief finally killed him.

sentences.zh: 周琬，江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhou Wan was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wan came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，父為滁州牧，坐罪論死。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era his father was prefect of Chuzhou; for a crime he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign his father served as prefect of Chuzhou, but after committing a crime was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 琬年十六，叩閽請代。

translations.literal: Wan at sixteen knocked on the palace gate requesting to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Wan went to the palace gate and begged to die in his father's stead.

sentences.zh: 帝疑受人教，命斬之，琬顏色不變。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected someone had coached him and ordered him beheaded; Wan's countenance did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected someone had put him up to it and ordered him executed, but Wan's face never changed.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，命宥父死，謫戍邊。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at him, ordered his father spared from death, and banished him to border service.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by the boy's composure, the emperor spared his father's life and commuted the sentence to exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 琬復請曰：「戍與斬，均死爾。

translations.literal: Wan again petitioned, saying: "Exile service and beheading are both death alike.
translations.idiomatic: Wan petitioned again: "Frontier service and execution are both death all the same.

sentences.zh: 父死，子安用生為，顧就死以贖父戍。」

translations.literal: If father dies, what use is the son's living? I would rather go to death to redeem father's border banishment."
translations.idiomatic: If my father must die, what good is my life? Let me die instead and redeem his exile.

sentences.zh: 帝復怒，命縛赴市曹，琬色甚喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry again, ordered him bound and sent to the execution ground; Wan looked very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a fresh rage and had him bound for the execution ground, yet Wan looked almost glad.

sentences.zh: 帝察其誠，即赦之，親題禦屏曰「孝子周琬。」

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived his sincerity and at once pardoned him, personally inscribing on the imperial screen "Filial Son Zhou Wan."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his devotion was genuine, the emperor pardoned him at once and personally wrote on the imperial screen, "Filial Son Zhou Wan.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 同時子代父死者，更有虞宗濟、胡剛、陳圭。

translations.literal: At the same time those who as sons died in place of fathers furthermore included Yu Zongji, Hu Gang, and Chen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Other men of the same era who offered their lives for their fathers included Yu Zongji, Hu Gang, and Chen Gui.

sentences.zh: 宗濟，字思訓，常熟人。

translations.literal: Zongji, styled Sixun, was a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongji, who went by Sixun, was from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 父兄並有罪，吏將逮治。

translations.literal: Father and elder brother both had offenses; the clerks were about to seize them for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Both his father and elder brother stood accused, and the clerks were preparing to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 宗濟謂兄曰：「事涉徭役，國法嚴，往必死。

translations.literal: Zongji told his brother: "The matter involves corvée labor; state law is strict—if you go you will surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Zongji told his brother, "This concerns corvée labor, and the law is merciless. If you go, you will surely die.

sentences.zh: 父老矣，兄冢嗣，且未有後，我幸產兒，可代死。」

translations.literal: Father is old; elder brother is heir in the main line and as yet has no descendants; I fortunately have produced a son—I can die in your place."
translations.idiomatic: Father is old, you are the heir and still without a son, while I already have a child. Let me die in your stead.

sentences.zh: 乃挺身詣吏，白父兄無所預。

translations.literal: He then went forth in person to the clerks, declaring that father and elder brother had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the magistrates and declared that his father and brother had nothing to do with the offense.

sentences.zh: 吏疑而訊之，悉自引伏。

translations.literal: The clerks doubted and interrogated him; he fully confessed on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The officials questioned him suspiciously, but he confessed everything himself.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年竟斬於市，年二十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was finally beheaded in the marketplace at age twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In 1371 he was beheaded in the marketplace at the age of twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 剛，浙江新昌人。

translations.literal: Gang was a man of Xinchang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gang came from Xinchang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，父謫役泗上，以逃亡當死，敕駙馬都尉梅殷監刑。

translations.literal: Early in Hongwu his father was on penal labor along the Si River; for flight he was due to die; the Emperor ordered the Prince Consort Mei Yin to oversee the execution.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu his father was doing penal labor on the Si River. He had fled and was condemned to death, and the emperor ordered Prince Consort Mei Yin to supervise the execution.

sentences.zh: 剛時方走省，立河上俟渡。

translations.literal: Gang was then on a hurried visit home, standing by the river awaiting crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Gang happened to be visiting home at the time and was waiting on the riverbank to cross.

sentences.zh: 聞之，即解衣泅水而往，哀號泣代。

translations.literal: On hearing it, he at once shed his clothes, swam through the water, and went; wailing and weeping he asked to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the news he stripped off his clothes, swam the river, and rushed to the scene, wailing and begging to die in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 殷憫之，奏聞，詔宥其父，並宥同罪者八十二人。

translations.literal: Yin pitied him, memorialized the throne; an edict pardoned his father and also pardoned eighty-two men guilty of the same offense.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Yin reported the matter to the throne. An edict pardoned his father and, with him, eighty-two others convicted of the same offense.

sentences.zh: 圭，黃巖人。

translations.literal: Gui was a man of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 父為仇人所訐當死，圭詣闕上章曰：「臣為子不能諫父，致陷不義，罪當死，乞原父使自新。」

translations.literal: His father was denounced by an enemy and due to die; Gui went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject as a son could not remonstrate with his father, causing him to fall into injustice; the crime deserves death—I beg to spare father so he may reform."
translations.idiomatic: His father had been denounced by an enemy and was condemned to death. Gui went to the palace gate with a memorial: "As a son I failed to counsel my father and let him fall into wrongdoing. The fault is mine and I deserve to die. I beg you to spare my father so he may reform.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜曰：「不謂今日有此孝子，宜赦其父，俟四方朝覲官至，播告之，以風勵天下。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "I did not expect today such a filial son—his father should be pardoned; when officials from the four quarters arrive for court audience, proclaim it to inspire the world."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "I never thought to see such a filial son in my own day. His father should be pardoned. When officials from every region arrive for audience, proclaim this throughout the realm to stir others to virtue."

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書開濟奏曰：「罪有常刑，不宜屈法開僥幸路。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice Kai Ji memorialized: "Crimes have fixed penalties; one should not bend the law to open a path of lucky chance."
translations.idiomatic: But the Minister of Justice Kai Ji objected: "Every crime has its proper penalty. We must not bend the law and open a door to wishful thinking."

sentences.zh: 乃聽圭代，而戍其父雲南。

translations.literal: [The court] then allowed Gui to substitute, and exiled his father to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore accepted Gui's substitution and exiled his father to Yunnan instead.

sentences.zh: 十七年，左都御史詹徽奏言：「太平府民有毆孕婦至死者，罪當絞，其子請代。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui memorialized: "A commoner of Taiping Prefecture beat a pregnant woman to death—the crime warrants strangulation; his son asks to substitute."
translations.idiomatic: In 1384 the Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui reported: "A man in Taiping Prefecture beat a pregnant woman to death. The statute calls for strangulation, but his son asks to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 章下大理卿鄒俊議，曰：「子代父死，情固可嘉。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Chief Minister of Justice Zou Jun for deliberation; he said: "A son dying in father's place—emotionally it is indeed laudable.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Chief Minister of Justice Zou Jun, who wrote: "A son offering himself for his father is touching, and the feeling behind it is admirable.

sentences.zh: 然死婦系二人之命，冤曷由申；

translations.literal: Yet the dead woman was tied to two lives—how could her wrong be vindicated;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the murdered woman carried two lives within her. How would her grievance ever be answered?

sentences.zh: 犯人當二死之條，律何可貸。

translations.literal: the criminal falls under the statute for two deaths—how could the law be waived.
translations.idiomatic: The offender is liable under the statute for two deaths. How can the law be set aside?

sentences.zh: 與其存犯法之父，孰若全無罪之兒。」

translations.literal: Rather than preserve a law-breaking father, which is better than preserving a guiltless child."
translations.idiomatic: Better to spare an innocent son than to keep alive a father who has broken the law.

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 伍洪，字伯宏，安福人。

translations.literal: Wu Hong, styled Bohong, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hong, known as Bohong, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1371.

sentences.zh: 授績谿主簿，擢上元知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed clerk of Jixi, promoted to magistrate of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed clerk of Jixi and later promoted to magistrate of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，以母老不復仕。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when mourning ended, because his mother was old he did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and when the mourning term ended he refused further office because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 推資產與諸弟，而己獨隱居養母。

translations.literal: He pushed his assets to his younger brothers, while he alone lived in seclusion nourishing his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his property among his younger brothers and withdrew alone to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 有異母弟得罪逃，使者捕弗獲，執其母，洪哭訴求代。

translations.literal: A younger half-brother offended and fled; envoys could not seize him and took his mother; Hong wept and pleaded to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: A younger half-brother committed a crime and fled. When officers could not catch him they seized their mother instead. Hong wept and begged to take her place.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「汝往必死，莫若吾自當之。」

translations.literal: His mother said: "If you go you will surely die—better that I bear it myself."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "If you go you will certainly die. Better that I answer for this myself.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「安有子在而累母者。」

translations.literal: Hong said: "How could there be a son living yet burdening his mother?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong replied, "How can a son go on living while his mother bears the punishment?"

sentences.zh: 遂行，竟死於市。

translations.literal: He went forth at once and finally died in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once and was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 時有劉文煥者，廣濟人。

translations.literal: At the time there was Liu Wenhuan of Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time there was Liu Wenhuan of Guangji.

sentences.zh: 與兄文煇運糧愆期，當死。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Wenhui he transported grain past deadline—due to die.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Wenhui had delivered grain late and were both condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 兄以長坐，文煥詣吏請代，叩頭流血。

translations.literal: The elder brother by seniority bore the punishment; Wenhuan went to the clerks to substitute, knocking his head until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenhui was the elder, he was held responsible. Wenhuan went to the magistrates and begged to die in his place, knocking his forehead on the ground until blood ran.

sentences.zh: 所司上其狀，命宥之，則兄已死矣。

translations.literal: The office concerned reported his petition; an order pardoned him—but his elder brother was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The office reported his plea upward, and an edict granted mercy—but by then his brother was already dead.

sentences.zh: 太祖特書「義民」二字獎之。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor specially wrote the two characters "Righteous Commoner" to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor personally wrote the two words "Righteous Commoner" to honor him.

sentences.zh: 時京師有兄坐法，兩弟各自縛請代。

translations.literal: At the time in the capital an elder brother was under the law; two younger brothers each bound themselves and asked to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time in the capital an elder brother was condemned under the law, and two younger brothers each bound themselves and begged to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使問故，同詞對曰：「臣少失父，非兄無以至今日。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent an envoy to ask the reason; in the same words they replied: "We lost our father young—without our elder brother we could not have reached today.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor sent an envoy to ask why. Both gave the same answer: "We lost our father as children. Without our elder brother we could never have survived to this day.

sentences.zh: 兄當死，弟安敢愛其生。」

translations.literal: Elder brother is due to die—how dare younger brothers cherish their lives."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he must die, how can we younger brothers cling to our lives?

sentences.zh: 帝陽許之，而戒行刑者曰：「有難色者殺之，否則奏聞。」

translations.literal: The Emperor feigned assent, but warned the executioners: "Whoever shows distress—kill him; otherwise report to us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pretended to agree, then secretly told the executioners, "If either shows fear, kill him. If not, report back to me."

sentences.zh: 兩人皆引頸就刃，帝大嗟異，欲並其兄貰之。

translations.literal: Both stretched their necks toward the blade; the Emperor greatly sighed in wonder and wished to pardon all three brothers together.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers stretched out their necks for the blade. Deeply moved, the emperor wanted to pardon all three.

sentences.zh: 左都御史詹徽持不可，卒殺其兄。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui insisted it could not be done; in the end the elder brother was killed.
translations.idiomatic: But the Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui objected that the law could not be bent, and in the end the elder brother was executed.

sentences.zh: 朱煦，仙居人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu was a man of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu came from Xianju.

sentences.zh: 父季用，為福州知府。

translations.literal: His father Jiyong was prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiyong had served as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年詔盡逮天下積歲官吏為民害者，赴京師築城。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu an edict seized all officials of many years who had harmed the people and sent them to the capital to build the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In 1385 an edict ordered the arrest of long-serving officials throughout the empire who had oppressed the people and their dispatch to the capital for wall-building labor.

sentences.zh: 季用居官僅五月，亦被逮，病不能堪，謂煦曰：「吾辦一死耳，汝第收吾骨歸葬。」

translations.literal: Jiyong had been in office only five months and was also seized; illness unbearable, he told Xu: "I am resigned to death—you need only gather my bones and return them for burial."
translations.idiomatic: Jiyong had been in office only five months, yet he too was seized. Sick beyond endurance, he told Xu, "I am as good as dead. You need only collect my bones and carry them home for burial.

sentences.zh: 煦惶懼不敢頃刻離。

translations.literal: Xu was fearful and dared not leave for an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was terrified and would not leave his side for a moment.

sentences.zh: 時訴枉令嚴，訴而戍極邊者三人，抵極刑者四人矣。

translations.literal: At the time the order against wrongful appeals was strict: three who appealed were exiled to the farthest border; four who reached the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Appeals of injustice were forbidden under severe penalties: three men who appealed had already been exiled to the farthest frontier, and four had suffered the death penalty.
