sentences.zh: 煦奮曰：「訴不訴，等死耳，萬一父緣訴獲免，即戮死無恨。」

translations.literal: Xu roused himself and said: "To appeal or not—to appeal is death alike; if by chance father through appeal is spared, even if I am executed I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Xu steeled himself and said, "Whether I appeal or not, death is the same. If by some chance my father is spared through my plea, I will gladly die myself and feel no regret.

sentences.zh: 即具狀叩闕。

translations.literal: At once he prepared a petition and knocked on the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a petition at once and went to knock on the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖憫其意，赦季用，復其官。

translations.literal: The Taizu pitied his intent, pardoned Jiyong, and restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor was moved by his devotion, pardoned Jiyong, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 有危貞昉者，字孟陽，臨海諸生。

translations.literal: There was Wei Zhenfang, styled Mengyang, a student of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wei Zhenfang, known as Mengyang, a student from Linhai.

sentences.zh: 父孝先，洪武四年進士。

translations.literal: His father Xiaoxian was a jinshi of the fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaoxian had passed the metropolitan examination in 1371.

sentences.zh: 官陵川縣丞，坐法輸作江浦。

translations.literal: He served as assistant magistrate of Lingchuan; for a legal offense he was sentenced to labor at Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant magistrate of Lingchuan, but after a legal offense was sentenced to labor at Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 貞昉詣闕上疏曰：「臣父絓吏議輸作，筋力向衰，不任勞苦，而大母年逾九十，恐染霜露之疾，貽臣父終天之恨。

translations.literal: Zhenfang went to the palace gate with a memorial saying: "Your subject's father is caught in official proceedings and sentenced to labor; his sinews and strength are declining, unable to bear toil; moreover Grandmother is past ninety—I fear she will contract illness from frost and dew, leaving my father the grief of lifelong regret.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfang went to the palace gate with a memorial: "My father has been condemned to penal labor. His strength is failing and he cannot endure the work. My grandmother is more than ninety years old. I fear the cold will sicken her and leave my father with a grief he can never undo.

sentences.zh: 臣犬馬齒方壯，願代父作勞，俾父獲歸養，死且不朽。」

translations.literal: Your subject's dog-and-horse years are still vigorous—I wish to labor in father's place, that father may return to nourish her; even in death I would not perish."
translations.idiomatic: I am still young and strong. Let me labor in his place so he may return home to care for her. Even if I die, my name will not perish.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 貞昉力作不勝勞，閱七月病卒。

translations.literal: Zhenfang's forced labor could not bear the toil; after seven months he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfang could not endure the labor. Seven months later he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 劉謹，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Liu Jin was a man of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，父坐法戍雲南。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era his father for an offense was banished to garrison service in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign his father was convicted of a crime and exiled to military service in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 謹方六歲，問家人「雲南何在？」

translations.literal: Jin was just six years old and asked his household, "Where is Yunnan?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin was only six, he asked the people at home, "Where is Yunnan?

sentences.zh: 家人以西南指之，輒朝夕向之拜。

translations.literal: The household pointed southwest for him; morning and evening he bowed toward it.
translations.idiomatic: They pointed southwest; from then on he bowed toward that direction every morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 年十四，矍然曰：「雲南雖萬里，天下豈有無父之子哉！」

translations.literal: At age fourteen he started and said, "Though Yunnan is ten thousand li away, under heaven can there be a son without a father?"
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he said with sudden resolve, "Yunnan may lie ten thousand li away, but can there be a son under heaven who has no father?

sentences.zh: 奮身而往，閱六月抵其地，遇父於逆旅，相持號慟。

translations.literal: He threw himself into going; after six months he reached the place, met his father at a traveler's lodge, and they clung to each other wailing in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He set out with all his strength. Six months later he arrived, found his father at an inn, and they clung together, wailing in grief.

sentences.zh: 俄父患瘋痹，謹告官乞以身代。

translations.literal: Soon his father fell ill with paralysis; Jin reported to the officials and begged to substitute his own person.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his father was stricken with paralysis. Jin petitioned the authorities to take his father's place in exile.

sentences.zh: 法令戍邊者必年十六以上，嫡長男始許代。

translations.literal: The statute held that those garrisoned on the frontier must be sixteen or older; only the eldest legitimate son was permitted to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The law required border exiles to be at least sixteen, and only the eldest legitimate son could serve in a father's stead.

sentences.zh: 時謹未成丁，伯兄先死，乃歸家攜兄子往。

translations.literal: At the time Jin had not yet reached adulthood; his elder brother by birth had died first, so he returned home and took his brother's son with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was not yet of age, and his elder brother had already died, so he went home and brought his brother's son with him.

sentences.zh: 兄子亦弱未能自立，復歸悉鬻其產畀兄子，始獲奉其父還，孝養終身。

translations.literal: The brother's son was also weak and could not stand on his own; he returned again and sold all his property to give to the brother's son, and only then was able to bring his father back and filially support him to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew was too young to support himself. Jin went back, sold everything he owned, and gave it all to the nephew; only then could he bring his father home and care for him filially for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 李德成，浹水人。

translations.literal: Li Decheng was a man of Jiaoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Decheng was from Jiaoshui.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父。

translations.literal: In youth he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father in childhood.

sentences.zh: 元末，年十二，隨母避寇至河濱。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, when he was twelve, he followed his mother fleeing bandits to the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Yuan, at age twelve, he fled bandits with his mother to the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 寇騎迫，母投河死。

translations.literal: Bandit horsemen pressed close; his mother threw herself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit horsemen closed in; his mother threw herself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 德成長，娶婦王氏。

translations.literal: When Decheng grew up, he took a wife, the Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: When Decheng came of age, he married a woman of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 摶土為父母像，與妻朝夕事之。

translations.literal: He molded earth into images of his parents, and with his wife served them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He molded clay images of his parents, and he and his wife tended them morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 方嚴冬，大雪，水堅至河底。

translations.literal: It was deep winter; heavy snow fell, and the water froze solid to the riverbed.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep winter. Snow fell heavily, and the river froze to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 德成夢母曰：「我處水下，寒不得出。」

translations.literal: Decheng dreamed his mother said, "I am beneath the water; the cold will not let me out."
translations.idiomatic: Decheng dreamed that his mother said, "I am under the water. The cold will not let me out.

sentences.zh: 覺而大慟，旦與妻徒跣行三百里，抵河濱。

translations.literal: On waking he wailed greatly; at dawn he and his wife went barefoot three hundred li and reached the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: He woke in anguish. At dawn he and his wife walked three hundred li barefoot to the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 臥水七日，水果融數十丈，恍惚若見其母，而他處堅凍如故。

translations.literal: He lay on the water seven days; the ice then melted for several tens of zhang, and dimly he seemed to see his mother, while elsewhere the ice stayed frozen as before.
translations.idiomatic: He lay on the ice seven days. The river opened for dozens of yards around him, and he seemed dimly to see his mother, while everywhere else the ice remained as hard as before.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃歸。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he returned home.

sentences.zh: 洪武十九年舉孝廉，屢擢尚寶丞。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 19 he was recommended as a filial and incorrupt candidate and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasures.

sentences.zh: 二十七年旌為孝子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was commended as a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he was honored as an exemplar of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 建文中，燕兵逼濟南。

translations.literal: Under the Jianwen reign, Yan's troops pressed upon Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign, the Prince of Yan's army pressed upon Jinan.

sentences.zh: 德成往諭令還兵，燕兵不退。

translations.literal: Decheng went to admonish them and order them to withdraw; the Yan troops did not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Decheng went to urge them to withdraw; the Yan army did not retreat.

sentences.zh: 德成歸，以辱命下吏，已而釋之。

translations.literal: Decheng returned; for disgracing his commission he was handed to the judicial officers, but was soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Decheng returned. For failing his mission he was handed over to the magistrates, but was soon released.

sentences.zh: 永樂初復官，屢遷陜西布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle his office was restored; he was repeatedly promoted to Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongle reign his office was restored, and he rose repeatedly to Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沈德四，直隸華亭人。

translations.literal: Shen Desi was a man of Huating in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Desi was from Huating in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 祖母疾，刲股療之愈。

translations.literal: When his grandmother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to treat her and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to heal her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 己而祖父疾，又刲肝作湯進之，亦愈。

translations.literal: Later when his grandfather fell ill, he again cut his liver, made broth, and presented it; he too recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandfather later fell ill, he cut out part of his liver, made broth, and fed it to him; he too recovered.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年被旌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu he received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 26 he was publicly commended.

sentences.zh: 尋授太常贊禮郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Assistant Master of Ceremonies in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Assistant Master of Ceremonies in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上元姚金玉、昌平王德兒亦以刲肝愈母疾，與德四同旌。

translations.literal: Shangyuan's Yao Jinyu and Changping's Wang De'er also, by cutting the liver, cured their mothers' illnesses, and were commended together with Desi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jinyu of Shangyuan and Wang De'er of Changping likewise cured their mothers by cutting out their own liver; they were honored together with Desi.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年九月，山東守臣言：「日照民江伯兒，母疾，割肋肉以療，不愈。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year, ninth month, the Shandong frontier official reported: "The Rizhao commoner Jiang Bo'er—his mother was ill; he cut flesh from his ribs to treat her, but she did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 27 the Shandong frontier official reported: "Jiang Bo'er, a commoner of Rizhao, cut flesh from his ribs to treat his mother's illness, but she did not recover.

sentences.zh: 禱岱嶽神，母疾瘳，願殺子以祀。

translations.literal: He prayed to the god of Mount Tai; his mother's illness was cured, and he vowed to kill his son as a sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to the god of Mount Tai. When his mother recovered, he vowed to kill his son as an offering.

sentences.zh: 已果瘳，竟殺其三歲兒。」

translations.literal: When she had indeed recovered, he finally killed his three-year-old son."
translations.idiomatic: She did recover, and in the end he killed his three-year-old son.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「父子天倫至重。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and said, "The bond between father and son is of the utmost weight in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious. "The bond between father and son is the weightiest tie in human relations," he said.

sentences.zh: 《禮》父服長子三年。

translations.literal: The Rites prescribe that a father mourn his eldest son for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites prescribe that a father mourn his eldest son for three years.

sentences.zh: 今小民無知，滅倫害理，亟宜治罪。」

translations.literal: Now ignorant commoners destroy human relations and harm principle; they should be punished at once."
translations.idiomatic: These ignorant commoners have destroyed human bonds and violated moral principle. They must be punished without delay.

sentences.zh: 遂逮伯兒，仗之百，遣戍海南。

translations.literal: He thereupon arrested Bo'er, beat him one hundred strokes with the staff, and sent him into exile in Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: He had Bo'er arrested, beaten one hundred strokes with the staff, and exiled to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 因命議旌表例。

translations.literal: He then ordered discussion of the regulations for commendation and public honor.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate on the rules for commendation.

sentences.zh: 禮臣議曰：「人子事親，居則致其敬，養則致其樂，有疾則醫藥籲禱，迫切之情，人子所得為也。

translations.literal: The ritual officials deliberated and said, "A son serving his parents: in residence he should bring them reverence; in support he should bring them joy; when they are ill he should give medicine and earnest prayer—the urgent feelings a son may properly show.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials submitted: "In serving parents, a son should show reverence in daily life and joy in their care; when they fall ill he may give medicine and pray with all his heart. Such urgent devotion is what a son may properly offer.

sentences.zh: 至臥冰割股，上古未聞。

translations.literal: As for lying on ice or cutting flesh from the thigh, antiquity never heard of such things.
translations.idiomatic: Lying on ice or cutting flesh from one's thigh—antiquity never heard of such things.

sentences.zh: 倘父母止有一子，或割肝而喪生，或臥冰而致死，使父母無依，宗祀永絕，反為不孝之大。

translations.literal: If parents have only one son, and by cutting the liver one loses one's life, or by lying on ice one dies, leaving parents without support and the ancestral sacrifices cut off forever, that becomes the greatest filial impiety instead.
translations.idiomatic: If parents have only one son, and he dies cutting out his liver or lying on ice, leaving them unsupported and the ancestral line extinguished forever, that is the greatest filial impiety of all.

sentences.zh: 皆由愚昧之徒，尚詭異，駭愚俗，希旌表，規避裏徭。

translations.literal: All this comes from ignorant persons who prize the bizarre, shock the foolish populace, hope for commendation, and scheme to evade village corvée.
translations.idiomatic: All this springs from ignorant men who prize the bizarre, shock common people, hope for public honor, and scheme to escape village corvée.

sentences.zh: 割股不已，至於割肝，割肝不已，至於殺子。

translations.literal: Cutting the thigh did not stop; it reached cutting the liver; cutting the liver did not stop; it reached killing a child.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting the thigh was not enough—they went on to cutting the liver; cutting the liver was not enough—they went on to killing a child.

sentences.zh: 違道傷生，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Violating the Way and harming life—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing violates the Way or destroys life more gravely than this.

sentences.zh: 自今父母有疾，療治罔功，不得已而臥冰割股，亦聽其所為，不在旌表例。」

translations.literal: From now on, when parents are ill and treatment has no effect, if there is no alternative but to lie on ice or cut the thigh, they may also be allowed to do as they will, but such acts are not within the regulations for commendation."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when parents are ill and medicine fails, if there is truly no alternative but to lie on ice or cut the thigh, let them do as they must—but such acts shall not fall under the rules for commendation.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The decree said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The decree read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 永樂間，江陰衛卒徐佛保等復以割股被旌。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, Jiangyin Guard soldier Xu Fobao and others were again commended for cutting the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Xu Fobao of Jiangyin Guard and others were again commended for cutting flesh from their thighs.

sentences.zh: 而掖縣張信、金吾右衛總旗張法保援李德成故事，俱擢尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Yexian's Zhang Xin and the Chief Banner of the Right Gold Guard Zhang Fabao, citing Li Decheng's precedent, were both promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Yexian's Zhang Xin and Chief Banner Zhang Fabao of the Right Gold Guard, citing Li Decheng's precedent, were both promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasures.

sentences.zh: 迨英、景以還，即割股者亦格於例，不以聞，而所旌，大率皆廬墓者矣。

translations.literal: From the Ying and Jing reigns onward, even those who cut the thigh were barred by regulation and not reported; what was commended was for the most part those who kept vigil at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ying and Jing reigns onward, even thigh-cutting was excluded by regulation and no longer reported upward; honors went mostly to those who mourned at the grave.

sentences.zh: 謝定住，大同廣昌人。

translations.literal: Xie Dingzhu was a man of Guangchang in Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Dingzhu was from Guangchang in Datong.

sentences.zh: 年十二，家失牛。

translations.literal: At age twelve the family lost an ox.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve the family lost an ox.

sentences.zh: 母抱幼子追逐，定住隨母後。

translations.literal: His mother, holding the infant son, ran in pursuit; Dingzhu followed behind his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother took the baby and ran after it; Dingzhu followed behind her.

sentences.zh: 虎躍出噬其母，定住奮前擊之，虎逸去。

translations.literal: A tiger leaped out and seized his mother to devour her; Dingzhu rushed forward and struck it, and the tiger fled.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger leaped out to seize his mother. Dingzhu rushed forward and struck it, and the tiger fled.

sentences.zh: 取弟抱之，扶母行。

translations.literal: He picked up his younger brother and carried him, and supported his mother as they walked.
translations.idiomatic: He picked up his younger brother, helped his mother walk on, and carried the child.

sentences.zh: 虎復追嚙母頸，定住再擊之，虎復去。

translations.literal: The tiger pursued again and bit his mother's neck; Dingzhu struck it again, and the tiger left once more.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger came back and bit his mother's neck. Dingzhu struck again, and the tiger withdrew.

sentences.zh: 行數武，虎還嚙母足。

translations.literal: After going several paces, the tiger returned and bit his mother's foot.
translations.idiomatic: They had gone only a few paces when the tiger returned and bit her foot.

sentences.zh: 定住復取石擊，虎乃舍去，母子三人並全。

translations.literal: Dingzhu again took up stones and struck; the tiger then let go and left, and mother and the three children were all preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhu seized stones and struck again. The tiger let go and left. Mother and all three children survived.

sentences.zh: 永樂十二年，帝召見嘉獎，賜米十石、鈔二百錠，旌其門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongle the Emperor summoned him, praised and rewarded him, granted ten shi of grain and two hundred ingots of paper money, and honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 12 the Emperor summoned him, praised and rewarded him, granted ten shi of grain and two hundred ingots of paper money, and honored his household gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，洪武中，有包實夫者，進賢人。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Hongwu reign, there was Bao Shifu, a man of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Hongwu reign, there was Bao Shifu of Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 授徒數十里外，途遇虎，銜衣入林中，釋而蹲。

translations.literal: He was teaching pupils several tens of li away; on the road he met a tiger that seized his robe and carried him into the woods, released him, and crouched.
translations.idiomatic: He was teaching pupils several tens of li from home when he met a tiger on the road. It seized his robe, dragged him into the woods, released him, and crouched.

sentences.zh: 實夫拜請曰：「吾被食，命也，如父母失養何？」

translations.literal: Shifu bowed and pleaded, "If I am eaten, it is fate—but what if my parents lose their support?"
translations.idiomatic: Shifu bowed and pleaded, "If I am eaten, that is fate—but what will become of my parents?

sentences.zh: 虎即舍去。

translations.literal: The tiger at once let go and left.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger at once let go and left.

sentences.zh: 後人名其地為拜虎岡。

translations.literal: Later people named the place Tiger-Bowing Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations named the place Tiger-Bowing Ridge.

sentences.zh: 其後，嘉靖中，筠連諸生蘇奎章，從父入山，猝遇虎。

translations.literal: Afterward, in the Jiajing reign, the Junlian student Su Kuizhang followed his father into the mountains and suddenly met a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Jiajing reign, the Junlian student Su Kuizhang went into the mountains with his father and suddenly met a tiger.

sentences.zh: 奎章倉皇泣告，願舍父食己，虎曳尾徐去。

translations.literal: Kuizhang in panic wept and declared he would give up his father and let himself be eaten; the tiger dragged its tail and slowly departed.
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhang wept in panic and offered himself in his father's place. The tiger lowered its tail and walked slowly away.

sentences.zh: 後為岷府教授。

translations.literal: Later he became Instructor in the Princedom of Min.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Instructor in the Princedom of Min.

sentences.zh: 權謹，字仲常，徐州人。

translations.literal: Quan Jin, style name Zhongchang, was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jin, style name Zhongchang, was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲喪父，即哀毀，奉母至孝。

translations.literal: At ten he lost his father and at once grieved in ruin; he served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at ten and mourned with devastating grief; he served his mother with utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年薦授樂安知縣，遷光祿署丞，以省侍歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Le'an, transferred to Deputy Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and returned home to attend his mother in reduced service.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 4 he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Le'an, then transferred to Deputy Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he returned home on leave to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母年九十終，廬墓三年，致泉湧免馴之異。

translations.literal: When his mother died at ninety he kept vigil at the grave three years, and there appeared the marvels of a spring gushing forth and tame hares.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died at ninety he kept vigil at her grave three years, and marvels appeared—a spring burst forth and hares grew tame.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，仁宗命馳驛赴闕，出其事狀，令侍臣朗誦大廷，以示百僚，即拜文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: The local authorities reported it; Emperor Renzong ordered him rushed by post to court, produced the account of his deeds, and had attending ministers read it aloud in the great hall to show the hundred officials; he was at once appointed Grand Academician of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported the matter. Emperor Renzong ordered him rushed to court by post relay, had his deeds read aloud in the great hall for all officials to hear, and appointed him Grand Academician of the Wenhua Hall on the spot.

sentences.zh: 謹辭，帝曰：「朕擢卿以風天下為子者，他非卿責也。」

translations.literal: Jin declined; the Emperor said, "I have raised you to instruct all under heaven who are sons—other matters are not your charge."
translations.idiomatic: Jin declined. The Emperor said, "I have elevated you to set an example for sons everywhere. Other duties are not your charge.

sentences.zh: 尋扈從皇太子監國南京。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed the Crown Prince in overseeing the realm from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he accompanied the Crown Prince in governing the realm from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嗣位，以疾乞歸，改通政司右參議，賜白金文綺致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, he begged leave on grounds of illness; he was changed to Right Vice Commissioner in the Office of Transmission, and was granted white gold and patterned silks on retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, he begged leave on grounds of illness, was reassigned as Right Vice Commissioner in the Office of Transmission, and retired with gifts of white gold and patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 子倫，舉永樂中鄉試。

translations.literal: His son Lun passed the provincial examination in the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun passed the provincial examination during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 養親二十年，親終不仕。

translations.literal: He supported his parents twenty years; when they died he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his parents for twenty years and never took office after they died.

sentences.zh: 倫子宇，父母卒，皆廬墓。

translations.literal: Lun's son Yu, when both parents died, kept vigil at the grave for each.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's son Yu likewise kept vigil at the grave when each parent died.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年亦獲旌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua he too received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 12 he too was publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 趙紳，字以行，諸暨人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shen, style name Yixing, was a man of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shen, style name Yixing, was from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 父秩，永樂中為高郵州學正，考滿赴京，至武城縣墮水。

translations.literal: His father Zhi, in the Yongle reign, was Director of Studies in Gaoyou Prefecture; when his term ended he went to the capital, and at Wucheng County fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi served as Director of Studies in Gaoyou Prefecture during the Yongle reign. When his term ended he traveled to the capital and fell into the water at Wucheng County.

sentences.zh: 紳奮身下救，河流湍悍，俱不能出。

translations.literal: Shen threw himself in to rescue him; the river current was fierce and swift, and neither could get out.
translations.idiomatic: Shen leaped in to save him, but the current was fierce and neither could escape.

sentences.zh: 明日屍浮水上，紳兩手抱父臂不釋。

translations.literal: The next day the corpses floated on the water; Shen's two hands still embraced his father's arm and did not release.
translations.idiomatic: The next day their bodies floated to the surface. Shen still clasped his father's arm with both hands and would not let go.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年旌其門。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande his gate was honored.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 his household gate was honored.

sentences.zh: 有向化者，靜海衛人。

translations.literal: There was one Xiang Hua, a man of Jinghai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xiang Hua of Jinghai Guard.

sentences.zh: 父上為衛指揮，墮海死。

translations.literal: His father Shang was a guard commander; he fell into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shang was a guard commander and drowned at sea.

sentences.zh: 化號泣求屍不得，亦投於海。

translations.literal: Hua wailed and sought the corpse but could not find it; he too threw himself into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Hua wept and searched for the body in vain, then threw himself into the sea as well.

sentences.zh: 忽父屍浮出，衣服盡脫。

translations.literal: Suddenly his father's corpse floated up; the clothes were entirely stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly his father's corpse rose to the surface, stripped of all clothing.

sentences.zh: 天方晴霽，雷雨驟作。

translations.literal: The sky had just cleared after rain when thunder and rain burst forth at once.
translations.idiomatic: The sky had just cleared when thunder and rain broke out at once.

sentences.zh: 既息，化首頂父衣，浮至一處。

translations.literal: When it ceased, Hua bore his father's garment on his head and floated to a certain place.
translations.idiomatic: When the storm passed, Hua bore his father's garment on his head and drifted ashore.

sentences.zh: 眾異而收葬之。

translations.literal: The crowd marveled and gathered the remains for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers marveled and gathered the remains for burial.

sentences.zh: 陸尚質者，山陰人。

translations.literal: Lu Shangzhi was a man of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shangzhi was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父渡江遇風，飄舟將入海。

translations.literal: His father crossed the river and met wind; the drifting boat was about to enter the open sea.
translations.idiomatic: His father crossed the river into a gale; the boat was being driven out to sea.

sentences.zh: 尚質自崖見之，即躍入濤中，欲挽舟近岸。

translations.literal: Shangzhi saw it from the cliff and at once leaped into the billows, wishing to draw the boat near the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi saw it from the cliff, leaped into the waves, and tried to pull the boat toward shore.

sentences.zh: 父舟獲濟，而尚質竟溺死。

translations.literal: His father's boat was saved, but Shangzhi in the end drowned.
translations.idiomatic: His father's boat reached safety, but Shangzhi drowned.

sentences.zh: 裏人呼其處為陸郎渡。

translations.literal: Villagers call the place Young Master Lu's Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers still call the place Young Master Lu's Crossing.

sentences.zh: 麹祥，字景德，永平人。

translations.literal: Qu Xiang, style name Jingde, was a man of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Xiang, style name Jingde, was from Yongping.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，父亮為金山衛百戶。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign his father Liang was a company commander at Jinshan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign his father Liang was a company commander at Jinshan Guard.

sentences.zh: 祥年十四，被倭掠。

translations.literal: When Xiang was fourteen he was seized by Japanese raiders.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Xiang was seized by Japanese raiders.

sentences.zh: 國王知為中國人，召侍左右，改名元貴，遂仕其國，有妻子，然心未嘗一日忘中國也，屢諷王入貢。

translations.literal: The king, knowing he was a man of China, summoned him to attend at his side, changed his name to Yuan Gui, and he then served that country, took wife and children, yet his heart never for one day forgot China, and repeatedly urged the king to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Learning he was Chinese, the king kept him at court, renamed him Yuan Gui, and he entered that country's service and raised a family there—yet never for a single day forgot China, and repeatedly urged the king to send tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，與使臣偕來，上疏言：「臣夙遭俘掠，抱釁痛心，流離困頓，艱苦萬狀。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he came with the envoys and submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject long ago suffered capture; bearing shame and grief in the heart, drifting in hardship and exhaustion through ten thousand forms of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande reign he came with the envoys and memorialized: "Your subject was long ago taken captive. I have borne shame and grief, wandered in exile, and endured hardships beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 今獲生還中國，夫豈由人。

translations.literal: Now I have obtained life and return to China—how could this be by human power alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have been granted life and return to China. Surely this is not merely by human effort.

sentences.zh: 伏乞賜歸侍養，不勝至願。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg to be permitted to return and serve in support; I cannot bear the utmost wish."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg permission to return home and care for my mother. I can scarcely express my longing.

sentences.zh: 天子方懷柔遠人，不從其請，但許給驛暫歸，仍還本國。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was then soothing distant peoples and did not grant his request, but allowed him post relays for a temporary return, still to go back to his original country.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then cultivating ties with distant peoples and denied his request, but allowed him post relays for a brief visit home before returning to his adopted country.

sentences.zh: 祥抵家，獨其母在，不能識，曰：「果吾兒，則耳陰有赤痣。」

translations.literal: When Xiang reached home, only his mother remained; she could not recognize him and said, "If you are truly my son, there is a red mole behind the ear."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang reached home only his mother remained. She could not recognize him and said, "If you are truly my son, there is a red mole behind your ear.

sentences.zh: 驗之信，抱持痛哭。

translations.literal: On verification it was true; they embraced and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He showed it; she believed, and they embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 未幾別去，至日本，啟以帝意。

translations.literal: Before long he took leave and departed; reaching Japan, he reported the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took leave and departed. Reaching Japan, he reported the Emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 國王允之，仍令入貢。

translations.literal: The king consented and still ordered him to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The king agreed and again ordered him to come on tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 祥乃復申前請，詔許襲職歸養。

translations.literal: Xiang then again submitted his former request; an edict permitted him to inherit his post and return home to support his parent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang renewed his earlier plea. An edict allowed him to inherit his father's military post and return home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母子相失二十年，又有華夷之限，竟得遂其初誌，聞者異之。

translations.literal: Mother and son had been separated twenty years, and there was moreover the barrier between Chinese and foreign realms; yet he finally fulfilled his first resolve—those who heard of it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son had been apart twenty years, separated by the gulf between China and a foreign land—yet he at last fulfilled the wish he had carried from the first. All who heard it marveled.
